cards.explanation: The answer is so they may live and take the land. Moses says he's teaching them “…so that you may live and may enter and take possession of the land that the LORD, the God of your fathers, is giving you.” The teaching has a purpose, friends, and it's a good one. Moses isn't just filling the air with words.

The answer is False. Moses says, “You must not add to or subtract from what I command you…” Nothing gets added and nothing gets cut, friends. The commands stay just as the LORD gave them, and Moses says the point is that they may keep the commandments of the LORD their God.

The answer is that every one of them is alive today. Moses says, “But you who held fast to the LORD your God are alive to this day, every one of you.” Not most of you. Not the lucky ones. EVERY one, friends. Right before that, he says the LORD destroyed all who followed Baal of Peor, a false god (Deuteronomy 4:3). Two groups, two outcomes, and the ones who held on are standing right there listening.

The answer is that they'll say this great nation is wise and understanding. Moses says the peoples will hear of all these statutes and say, “Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.” Wisdom is what shows, friends. Even people who aren't part of Israel take notice.
The word is near. Moses asks what nation has a god “…as near to them as the LORD our God is to us whenever we call on Him?” Whenever we call, He's near. Hold onto that one, friends.

The answer is the things their eyes have seen. Moses says, “…so that you do not forget the things your eyes have seen, and so that they do not slip from your heart as long as you live.” These are things Israel watched happen, friends. A memory like that is worth guarding.

The answer is True. Moses says, “Teach them to your children and grandchildren.” What Israel saw doesn't stop with them, friends. It's meant to be passed down to the next generation, and the one after that.

The mountain was blazing with fire up to the heavens. Moses describes it as “…a mountain blazing with fire to the heavens, with black clouds and deep darkness.” Imagine standing at the base of that, friends. I think I'd have held onto my hat with my mustache.
The answer is False. Moses says, “You heard the sound of the words but saw no form; there was only a voice.” A voice, and no form to look at, friends. Keep that in mind, because Moses leans on it.

The word is Commandments. Moses says the LORD declared His covenant, “…the Ten Commandments that He wrote on two tablets of stone.” The LORD wrote them on stone Himself, friends. That's about as clear as it gets.

The answer is an idol of any form or shape. Moses says, “…do not act corruptly and make an idol for yourselves of any form or shape…” Israel saw no form at Horeb, so no form of any kind should be made into an idol. The phrase "any form" covers a lot of ground, friends.

The answer is False. Moses lists a male or female, a beast on the earth, a bird that flies, a creature that crawls and a fish in the waters (Deuteronomy 4:16-18). Birds and fish are named on purpose, friends. He's covering every corner.

The answer is False. Moses says, “…do not be enticed to bow down and worship what the LORD your God has apportioned to all the nations under heaven.” No "…as long as…" is attached, friends. The sun, moon and stars aren't to be bowed down to.

The answer is the people of His inheritance. Moses says the LORD brought them out of Egypt, the iron furnace, “…to be the people of His inheritance, as you are today.” A furnace is a hot, hard place to be stuck, friends. The LORD didn't just open the door for Israel. He took them as His own.

The answer is True. Moses says he must die in this land, but then adds, “But you shall cross over and take possession of that good land.” He's not crossing, but the people are, friends. I think that was a heavy thing for him to say out loud, and he says it plainly.

The word is fire. Moses says, “For the LORD your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God.” He has just reminded them of the mountain blazing with fire, friends, so I think it lands hard. Moses doesn't soften it.

The answer is False. Moses says that if they act corruptly and make an idol, “You will not live long upon it, but will be utterly destroyed.” Before he says it, he calls heaven and earth as witnesses (Deuteronomy 4:26). It's a heavy warning, friends, and I think Moses means for it to be taken seriously.

The answer is that He would scatter them among the peoples. Moses says, “Then the LORD will scatter you among the peoples…” Scattered means spread out among other nations. That's the next thing he names, friends, and it's a hard one.

The answer is True. Moses says the LORD will scatter them among the peoples, “…and only a few of you will survive among the nations to which the LORD will drive you.” It's a sobering line, friends. I think this is one of the heavier parts of the sermon.

The answer is with all their heart and soul. Moses says, “But if from there you will seek the LORD your God, you will find Him if you seek Him with all your heart and with all your soul.” Even from far away, the way back is open, friends. All your heart, all your soul.

The word is merciful. Moses says, “For the LORD your God is a merciful God; He will not abandon you or destroy you or forget the covenant with your fathers, which He swore to them by oath.” After all those warnings, friends, this verse is a gift. Mercy gets the last word here.

The answer is that no other people has heard God's voice from the fire and lived. Moses asks, “Has a people ever heard the voice of God speaking out of the fire, as you have, and lived?” Heard and lived, friends. It's a question that expects one answer.

The answer is so they'd know the LORD alone is God. Moses says, “You were shown these things so that you would know that the LORD is God; there is no other besides Him.” That's the reason, friends, plain and simple. The trials, signs, wonders and war were all shown for that. Nothing added.

The answer is to discipline them. Moses says, “He let you hear His voice from heaven to discipline you…” He also showed them His great fire on earth, and they heard His words out of the fire, friends. The reason given is discipline.

The answer is because He loved their fathers. Moses says, “Because He loved your fathers, He chose their descendants after them and brought you out of Egypt by His presence and great power…” The reason is love, friends, plain and simple. Not size, not a record.

The answer is so they and their children may prosper in the land. Moses says, “Keep His statutes and commandments, which I am giving you today, so that you and your children after you may prosper, and that you may live long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you for all time.” That's the sermon brought home, friends. Moses names their children right in the verse, so this reaches past that one generation.
